content: 1. Magic words in MediaWiki are organized into an index. These words are used to perform specific functions or display specific text based on user input, denoted as XYZ in examples. 2. The tag `{{:}}` specifies text or function calls that are applied only on the transcluded page, not on the transcluding page. For instance, categorizing a template itself (and not the page where it is transcluded) would use this tag. 3. The tag `{{.}}` specifies text or function calls that are applied only on the transcluding page, not on the transcluded page (which is typically a template). For example, a template that categorizes pages where it is applied, but not the template itself, into a specific category would use this tag. 4. The tag `{{..}}` specifies text or function calls that are applied only on the transcluding page, not on the transcluded page. This tag differs from `{{:}}` in that any text or code on the transcluded page not enveloped by the tag will not be transcluded, regardless of whether the tag is in use. 5. The `{{categorytree}}` function provides a dynamic view of the category structure specified as a tree. 6. The `{{time}}` function displays the current time in UTC. However, if the page has not been edited or changed since the last time it was displayed by the same user, it may be cached by the user's browser, and the displayed time or date may not update. Similarly, if a heavily used page is retrieved from a caching system (e.g., the main page on Wikipedia), the date or time may not change from the last time it was retrieved by the caching hardware or software. 7. The `{{localtime}}` function displays the time based on the local timezone of the wiki, not the timezone set in the user's preferences. 8. Statistics variables in MediaWiki include thousands separators unless the `:R` modifier for raw is added. These variables are technically parser functions. 9. Parser functions like `{{DISPLAYTITLE}}` allow the page header to differ from the page name, and `{{DEFAULTSORT}}` sets a default category sort key for the page. 10. Formatting-related functions include references to language and template-specific lists, such as the list of Wikipedia local names. These lists show names for all languages without automatic comparison or highlight differences in names for specific languages. 11. Image modifiers in MediaWiki are used in links to adjust image properties. Some modifiers are mutually exclusive, and the last specified modifier takes precedence. 12. For framed images or thumbnails, the last unrecognized modifier is used as a caption or as a description for `alt` text. 13. Image position modifiers are mutually exclusive, with the last specified position taking precedence. Templates can stop floating for inline images, and only the `px` modifier is supported for inline images. 14. In PHP, the `$string` itself is oddly used as a condition for padding. This behavior is considered a bug and should be reported.
